_archived: ARCHIVED - not submitted, and not referenced by any flow.
Two reasons. First, the copy is stale: it describes ARM 2 as 'plain
language with clear answer options', which was true when ARM 2 printed a
numbered menu and asked people to type a digit. ARM 2 is now a tappable
list, and the flow's closing message says so. Submitting this would freeze
the older description permanently.
Second, and the reason it is not simply rewritten: this flow does not need
a closing template at all. A close only needs Meta approval if it can fall
outside the 24-hour window, and with 1-hour timeouts every path that
reaches a close has had an inbound reply within the last hour:
complete      last answer <= 1h ago       in session
declined      just replied                in session
incomplete    last answer <= 1h ago       in session
unreachable   never replied               no message sent at all
undeliverable message never arrived       no message sent at all
The last two are the ones that used to need this template, and they now
end silently instead - a message to someone who never opened the window
cannot be delivered, and there is nothing to thank a non-participant for.
The bookend rule in the whatsapp-template skill still stands for flows with
4-hour timeouts, where four questions can push the close past 24 hours.
Restore this file, update the copy, and submit it if you build one of those.
_comment: CLOSING template for the RST Jaipur 2026 data-use survey.
Sent as a template rather than free-form because the close fires after the
respondent has finished answering, which can be hours or days after they
started - the flow allows an hour per question. A participant who begins in
the afternoon and finishes the next morning is outside the 24-hour window,
and a free-form close would fail silently with 63016: they answer every
question and hear nothing back. As a template it delivers either way.
This is the second half of the bookend rule. The 2023 RST flow had no closing
The debrief is the point of the exercise: it reveals that participants were
randomised into two question formats, which is what makes the session teach
something. Registration is handled separately, so this teases the results
No variables, so nothing to get wrong at send time.

twilio/text.body:
Thank you for completing the survey.

You took part in an experiment with two different versions of the same survey: one using plain language with clear answer options, and one more open and complex.

We want to show how the way a question is asked can change the answers - and the results - in WhatsApp surveys.

We will show what your group's answers looked like, live in the session. See you there.

_IPA Team_
